title: Psalms Chapter 22 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 22 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 22 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 22.

questions.question: In Psalms 22, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
But thou art holy, O thou that inhabitest the praises of Israel.
They cried unto thee, and were delivered.
I was cast upon thee from the womb.
questions.correctAnswer: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
questions.explanation: This phrase is the opening line of the chapter, making it the first event mentioned.

questions.question: What does the psalmist express about his cries in the daytime?
options: They are heard by God.
They are not heard by God.
They are joyful cries.
They are for help.
questions.correctAnswer: They are not heard by God.
questions.explanation: The psalmist states, 'O my God, I cry in the daytime, but thou hearest not;' indicating his cries are unheard.

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe God in Psalms 22:3?
options: A reproach of men
Holy
Far from helping
A worm
questions.correctAnswer: Holy
questions.explanation: The psalmist refers to God as 'holy,' acknowledging His nature.

questions.question: What did the fathers do in relation to God according to Psalms 22:4?
options: They cried unto thee.
They were confounded.
They laughed to scorn.
They turned away.
questions.correctAnswer: They cried unto thee.
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Our fathers trusted in thee: they trusted, and thou didst deliver them.'

questions.question: What was the result for those who cried unto God according to Psalms 22:5?
options: They were not delivered.
They were delivered.
They were confounded.
They were mocked.
questions.correctAnswer: They were delivered.
questions.explanation: The verse clearly states, 'They cried unto thee, and were delivered.'

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe himself in Psalms 22:6?
options: A king
A worm
A mighty warrior
An angel
questions.correctAnswer: A worm
questions.explanation: The psalmist says, 'But I am a worm, and no man;' indicating his lowly status.

questions.question: What do those who see the psalmist do according to Psalms 22:7?
options: Help him
Laugh him to scorn
Praise him
Ignore him
questions.correctAnswer: Laugh him to scorn
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'All they that see me laugh me to scorn.'

questions.question: What do the mockers say about the psalmist in Psalms 22:8?
options: Let him deliver himself.
He is a king.
He is blessed.
He is forsaken.
questions.correctAnswer: Let him deliver himself.
questions.explanation: The mockers challenge the psalmist by saying, 'He trusted on the LORD that he would deliver him: let him deliver him.'

questions.question: What did God do when the psalmist was born according to Psalms 22:9?
options: He made him hope.
He abandoned him.
He cast him away.
He blessed him.
questions.correctAnswer: He made him hope.
questions.explanation: The psalmist acknowledges that God 'didst make me hope when I was upon my mother's breasts.'

questions.question: From whom did the psalmist feel he was cast upon in Psalms 22:10?
options: His friends
The Lord
His family
His enemies
questions.correctAnswer: The Lord
questions.explanation: The psalmist states, 'I was cast upon thee from the womb: thou art my God from my mother's belly.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist plead for in Psalms 22:11?
options: Help from his enemies
Help from God
Silence from God
Distance from God
questions.correctAnswer: Help from God
questions.explanation: The psalmist requests, 'Be not far from me; for trouble is near; for there is none to help.'

questions.question: The psalmist feels abandoned by God.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: The psalmist opens with 'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?' signifying feelings of abandonment.

questions.question: The psalmist acknowledges God's holiness.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: In Psalms 22:3, the psalmist states, 'But thou art holy,' affirming God's holiness.

questions.question: The psalmist claims he is a mighty warrior.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The psalmist describes himself as 'a worm, and no man;' not as a mighty warrior.

questions.question: The psalmist feels he has many helpers.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: The psalmist states, 'for there is none to help.' indicating he feels alone.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 22 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 22 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Psalms 22:12, who has compassed the psalmist?
options: Many bulls: strong bulls of Bashan
Lions from the forest
Wolves from the mountains
Serpents from the desert
questions.correctAnswer: Many bulls: strong bulls of Bashan
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:12 states, 'Many bulls have compassed me: strong bulls of Bashan have beset me round.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 22:21 promise will happen if someone calls for deliverance as commanded in Psalms 22:20?
options: They will be saved from the lion's mouth
They will be surrounded by many bulls
They will be mocked by their enemies
They will have their garments parted
questions.correctAnswer: They will be saved from the lion's mouth
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:20 commands deliverance, and Psalms 22:21 promises, 'Save me from the lion's mouth: for thou hast heard me from the horns of the unicorns.'

questions.question: In Psalms 22:15, what physical condition does the psalmist describe as a result of his suffering?
options: My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws
My bones are strengthened and my heart is firm
My hands and feet are untouched by pain
My garments are clean and unparted
questions.correctAnswer: My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws
questions.explanation: Verse 15 describes the psalmist's suffering: 'My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws.'

questions.question: How do Psalms 22:16 and 22:17 together describe the psalmist's enemies' actions?
options: They pierced my hands and feet; they look and stare upon me
They healed my wounds; they covered me with kindness
They fled at my approach; they blessed me
They ignored me completely; they turned their backs
questions.correctAnswer: They pierced my hands and feet; they look and stare upon me
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:16 says, 'they pierced my hands and my feet,' and Psalms 22:17 adds, 'they look and stare upon me,' showing the enemies' cruel actions.

questions.question: What does the psalmist request from the LORD in Psalms 22:19?
options: Be not thou far from me; O my strength, haste thee to help me
Deliver me from the sword
I will declare thy name unto my brethren
Many bulls have compassed me
questions.correctAnswer: Be not thou far from me; O my strength, haste thee to help me
questions.explanation: In Psalms 22:19 the psalmist pleads, 'But be not thou far from me, O LORD: O my strength, haste thee to help me.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 22:18, what do the enemies do with the psalmist's garments?
options: They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture
They protect my garments from harm
They return my garments to me
They burn my garments completely
questions.correctAnswer: They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:18 says, 'They part my garments among them, and cast lots upon my vesture,' describing the enemies' actions.

questions.question: In Psalms 22:14, how does the psalmist describe his heart amidst his suffering?
options: My heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels
My heart is strong and unyielding
My heart is joyful and singing
My heart is hardened like stone
questions.correctAnswer: My heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels
questions.explanation: Verse 14 clearly states, 'my heart is like wax; it is melted in the midst of my bowels,' illustrating his emotional anguish.

questions.question: What analogy does the psalmist use in Psalms 22:13 to describe his enemies' behavior?
options: They gaped upon me with their mouths, as a ravening and a roaring lion
They whispered softly like doves
They stood silently like stones
They sang praises like angels
questions.correctAnswer: They gaped upon me with their mouths, as a ravening and a roaring lion
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:13 uses the imagery of fierce lions to depict the enemies: 'They gaped upon me with their mouths, as a ravening and a roaring lion.'

questions.question: What does the psalmist promise to do in the midst of the congregation according to Psalms 22:22?
options: I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee
I will remain silent and keep my pain hidden
I will curse my enemies loudly
I will turn away from the LORD
questions.correctAnswer: I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:22 states the psalmist's intention to praise God publicly: 'I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee.'

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe his physical state in Psalms 22:14 and what might this teach about expressing weakness before God?
options: He is poured out like water, with bones out of joint and a melting heart; teaching that honest expression of suffering invites God's presence
He is strong and unshaken; teaching that weakness should be hidden
He is victorious and joyful; teaching to focus only on blessings
He is indifferent to his pain; teaching detachment
questions.correctAnswer: He is poured out like water, with bones out of joint and a melting heart; teaching that honest expression of suffering invites God's presence
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:14 describes intense suffering, illustrating that genuine vulnerability before God is part of faithful prayer.

questions.question: What practical lesson on prayer can be drawn from the contrast between Psalms 22:1 and Psalms 22:19?
options: Even when feeling forsaken, the psalmist urges God not to be far and to hasten help, showing persistent faith in prayer
Prayer should be abandoned when no answer is heard
God is distant and uncaring, so prayer is useless
Only silent meditation is effective, not vocal prayer
questions.correctAnswer: Even when feeling forsaken, the psalmist urges God not to be far and to hasten help, showing persistent faith in prayer
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:1 expresses feeling forsaken, but Psalms 22:19 immediately asks God not to be far and to help quickly, demonstrating persistent faith.

questions.question: Considering Psalms 22:16 and 22:18, what attitude towards suffering and injustice might a believer cultivate?
options: Trust in God's justice despite enemies' piercing and dividing actions
Retaliate immediately against enemies
Ignore suffering and pretend all is well
Seek revenge by casting lots with enemies
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God's justice despite enemies' piercing and dividing actions
questions.explanation: Though enemies pierce and divide garments (22:16-18), the psalmist prays for deliverance, implying trust in God's justice amid injustice.

questions.question: What does the psalmist's description in Psalms 22:17 about bones suggest about vulnerability in faith?
options: He may tell all his bones because enemies stare, showing openness even in exposure
He hides his pain and weakness from others
He pretends to be strong before enemies
He denies his suffering entirely
questions.correctAnswer: He may tell all his bones because enemies stare, showing openness even in exposure
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:17 says, 'I may tell all my bones: they look and stare upon me,' indicating the psalmist's openness despite vulnerability.

questions.question: How does the phrase in Psalms 22:20 about 'my darling from the power of the dog' figuratively apply to Christian prayer for protection?
options: It represents asking God to protect what is precious from evil
It means literally rescuing a pet dog
It suggests ignoring danger completely
It encourages trusting in human strength alone
questions.correctAnswer: It represents asking God to protect what is precious from evil
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:20 requests God to 'Deliver my soul from the sword; my darling from the power of the dog,' figuratively seeking divine protection of what is valuable.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 22:12 describes the psalmist being surrounded by gentle and kind animals.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:12 states the psalmist is compassed by 'Many bulls: strong bulls of Bashan,' indicating strength and threat, not gentleness.

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 22 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 22.

questions.question: According to Psalms 22:23, who are called to praise and glorify the LORD?
options: Ye that fear the LORD; all ye the seed of Jacob; all ye the seed of Israel
The kings and priests of Israel
The prophets and the priests
All the nations of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Ye that fear the LORD; all ye the seed of Jacob; all ye the seed of Israel
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:23 explicitly calls 'Ye that fear the LORD, praise him; all ye the seed of Jacob, glorify him; and fear him, all ye the seed of Israel.'

questions.question: What does Psalms 22:24 say about God's response to the afflicted who cry unto Him?
options: He hath not despised nor abhorred the affliction; He heard when they cried
He sometimes hides His face and does not hear
He delays in hearing their cries
He punishes the afflicted for their sins
questions.correctAnswer: He hath not despised nor abhorred the affliction; He heard when they cried
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:24 states that God 'hath not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; neither hath he hid his face from him; but when he cried unto him, he heard.'

questions.question: In Psalms 22:25, before whom will the psalmist pay his vows?
options: Before them that fear him
Before the elders of Israel
Before the priests alone
Before the kings of the earth
questions.correctAnswer: Before them that fear him
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:25 says, 'My praise shall be of thee in the great congregation: I will pay my vows before them that fear him.'

questions.question: What promise is given to the meek in Psalms 22:26?
options: The meek shall eat and be satisfied; their heart shall live forever
The meek shall inherit the earth and rule over nations
The meek shall suffer but be comforted
The meek shall be exalted to kingship
questions.correctAnswer: The meek shall eat and be satisfied; their heart shall live forever
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:26 declares, 'The meek shall eat and be satisfied: they shall praise the LORD that seek him: your heart shall live for ever.'

questions.question: According to Psalms 22:27, who will remember, turn to the LORD, and worship before Him?
options: All the ends of the world and all the kindreds of the nations
Only Israel and the seed of Jacob
The priests and Levites
Only the righteous within Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: All the ends of the world and all the kindreds of the nations
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:27 states, 'All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the LORD: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee.'

questions.question: What is declared about the kingdom and governance in Psalms 22:28?
options: The kingdom is the LORD's and He is the governor among the nations
The kingdom belongs to the kings of Israel
Governance is held by earthly rulers
The kingdom is divided among many gods
questions.correctAnswer: The kingdom is the LORD's and He is the governor among the nations
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:28 clearly affirms, 'For the kingdom is the LORD'S: and he is the governor among the nations.'

questions.question: What does the Hebrew word 'Yare' (ירא) in Psalms 22:23 generally mean?
options: To fear or revere
To love deeply
To rejoice greatly
To sacrifice
questions.correctAnswer: To fear or revere
questions.explanation: The Hebrew word 'Yare' (ירא) used in Psalms 22:23 is commonly translated as 'to fear or revere,' indicating reverence and awe towards God.

questions.question: Which literary device is prominently used in Psalms 22:14, 'I am poured out like water, and all my bones are out of joint'?
options: Simile
Metaphor
Hyperbole
Irony
questions.correctAnswer: Simile
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:14 uses a simile, comparing the psalmist's condition to water being poured out, illustrating extreme weakness and distress.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage echoes the theme of being forsaken by God as expressed in Psalms 22:1?
options: Matthew 27:46
John 3:16
Romans 8:28
Revelation 21:4
questions.correctAnswer: Matthew 27:46
questions.explanation: Matthew 27:46 records Jesus crying 'My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?' directly quoting Psalms 22:1, thus fulfilling the theme of abandonment.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage connects with Psalms 22:18 about garments being parted and lots cast?
options: Exodus 12:35
Genesis 37:23
Leviticus 16:8
questions.explanation: John 19:23-24 describes soldiers dividing Jesus’ garments and casting lots, echoing Psalms 22:18's prophecy.

questions.question: What immediately precedes the call to 'Ye that fear the LORD, praise him' in Psalms 22:23?
options: 'I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee.'
'Save me from the lion's mouth: for thou hast heard me.'
'For dogs have compassed me: the assembly of the wicked have inclosed me.'
'My strength is dried up like a potsherd; and my tongue cleaveth to my jaws.'
questions.correctAnswer: 'I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee.'
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:22 immediately precedes verse 23 with 'I will declare thy name unto my brethren: in the midst of the congregation will I praise thee.'

questions.question: How does Psalms 22:31 function as a typological prophecy in biblical theology?
options: It anticipates the gospel being declared to future generations
It predicts the destruction of Jerusalem
It describes the exile of Israel to Babylon
It focuses on the immediate deliverance of David
questions.correctAnswer: It anticipates the gospel being declared to future generations
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:31 speaks of declaring God's righteousness to people yet unborn, typologically pointing to the ongoing proclamation of God’s salvation through Christ to all generations.

questions.question: What type of parallelism is evident in Psalms 22:27, 'All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the LORD: and all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee'?
options: Synonymous parallelism
Antithetic parallelism
Synthetic parallelism
Emblematic parallelism
questions.correctAnswer: Synonymous parallelism
questions.explanation: Verse 27 uses synonymous parallelism, where the second line reinforces the first by repeating the idea with different wording.

questions.question: In Psalms 22:16, what is the significance of the phrase 'they pierced my hands and my feet' in textual and theological studies?
options: It is seen as a messianic prophecy fulfilled in the crucifixion of Jesus
It describes a literal hunting incident
It refers to physical punishment of David by Saul
It is metaphorical for emotional pain
questions.correctAnswer: It is seen as a messianic prophecy fulfilled in the crucifixion of Jesus
questions.explanation: The phrase in Psalms 22:16 is widely regarded as a prophetic foreshadowing of Jesus’ crucifixion where his hands and feet were pierced.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 22:29 teaches that none can keep alive his own soul.
options: True
False
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:29 states, 'none can keep alive his own soul,' affirming the truth of the statement.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 22 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 22 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 22:3 teach about God's nature?
options: God is holy and inhabits the praises of His people
God is distant and indifferent to human suffering
God is unknowable and hidden from mankind
God acts arbitrarily without regard for His covenant
questions.correctAnswer: God is holy and inhabits the praises of His people
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:3 states, 'But thou art holy, O thou that inhabitest the praises of Israel,' emphasizing God's holiness and His presence dwelling among the worship of His people.

questions.question: What doctrine about human sin and suffering is taught in Psalms 22:6?
options: Human beings are utterly despised and reproached in their sinfulness
Suffering is always a direct punishment from God
Human worth is independent of any divine perspective
Sin does not affect human dignity or relationship with God
questions.correctAnswer: Human beings are utterly despised and reproached in their sinfulness
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:6 says, 'But I am a worm, and no man; a reproach of men, and despised of the people,' expressing the deep abasement and shame associated with human sin and suffering.

questions.question: What doctrine of salvation does Psalms 22:24 teach?
options: God does not despise the afflicted and hears their cries for help
Salvation is earned by human merit and works
God is indifferent to the plight of the suffering
Deliverance is only for the righteous, never for the afflicted
questions.correctAnswer: God does not despise the afflicted and hears their cries for help
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:24 states, 'For he hath not despised nor abhorred the affliction of the afflicted; neither hath he hid his face from him; but when he cried unto him, he heard,' affirming God's attentive and compassionate salvation for the afflicted.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 3 specifically demonstrate?
options: Holiness
Omnipotence
Immutability
Justice
questions.correctAnswer: Holiness
questions.explanation: Verse 3 calls God 'holy,' highlighting His attribute of holiness as distinct and pure, dwelling among the praises of Israel.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does verse 28 specifically demonstrate?
options: Sovereignty
Omniscience
Mercy
Grace
questions.correctAnswer: Sovereignty
questions.explanation: Psalms 22:28 declares, 'For the kingdom is the LORD'S: and he is the governor among the nations,' illustrating God's sovereign rule over all nations.

questions.question: How does Psalms 22 connect to the New Testament passion narrative?
options: It prophetically describes the suffering and crucifixion of the Messiah
It recounts the resurrection of Christ directly
It narrates the early ministry of Jesus
It focuses primarily on Israel’s national history
questions.correctAnswer: It prophetically describes the suffering and crucifixion of the Messiah
questions.explanation: Psalm 22 contains vivid suffering imagery (e.g., pierced hands and feet, casting lots for garments) that the New Testament writers apply to Jesus' crucifixion (cf. John 19:23-24, Luke 23:34).

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Psalms 22:31 establish?
options: The proclamation of God's righteousness to future generations
The final judgement of the nations
The immediate restoration of Israel's monarchy
The cessation of all worship practices
questions.correctAnswer: The proclamation of God's righteousness to future generations
questions.explanation: Verse 31 says, 'They shall come, and shall declare his righteousness unto a people that shall be born,' indicating the ongoing witness to God's salvation across generations.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 1 and 24 teach about God's presence in suffering?
options: God may feel distant, but He does not ultimately forsake or ignore the afflicted
God abandons the faithful who suffer as a consequence of sin
Suffering proves God's absence and indifference
God's presence is only manifest when there is no suffering
questions.correctAnswer: God may feel distant, but He does not ultimately forsake or ignore the afflicted
questions.explanation: Verse 1 expresses a feeling of abandonment, while verse 24 affirms that God has not hidden His face but hears the cries, teaching that divine presence remains even amid suffering.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 16 and 18 teach about the Messiah's suffering?
options: The Messiah suffers physical torment and humiliation, fulfilling prophetic typology
The Messiah conquers without suffering or shame
The Messiah's suffering is symbolic without real pain
The Messiah is exalted above all suffering from the start
questions.correctAnswer: The Messiah suffers physical torment and humiliation, fulfilling prophetic typology
questions.explanation: Verse 16 speaks of pierced hands and feet, and verse 18 of dividing garments and casting lots, both pointing to detailed physical and humiliating suffering fulfilled in Christ’s crucifixion.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do verses 27 and 28 teach about God's universal reign and worship?
options: All nations will ultimately remember, turn to, and worship the LORD because He is sovereign
Only Israel will worship God, while nations remain rebellious
God's kingdom is limited to earthly Israel and does not extend globally
Worship is optional and not tied to God's kingship
questions.correctAnswer: All nations will ultimately remember, turn to, and worship the LORD because He is sovereign
questions.explanation: Verses 27 and 28 affirm that 'all the kindreds of the nations shall worship before thee' because 'the kingdom is the LORD’S,' teaching God’s universal sovereign reign and worship.

questions.question: What does Psalms 22:12-13 teach against the skeptical claim that God is powerless in human suffering?
options: The vivid depiction of surrounding enemies and danger underscores the reality of suffering but calls for God’s deliverance, not His impotence
God is indifferent and therefore powerless to intervene in suffering
Suffering is an illusion with no real spiritual cause
God causes suffering arbitrarily without purpose or power to save
questions.correctAnswer: The vivid depiction of surrounding enemies and danger underscores the reality of suffering but calls for God’s deliverance, not His impotence
questions.explanation: Verses 12-13 describe 'Many bulls' and 'a roaring lion' besetting the psalmist, illustrating real danger that calls for divine rescue, showing God’s power is needed and expected.

questions.question: What doctrine does Psalms 22:9 teach about God's covenant faithfulness from birth?
options: God’s covenant care and hope for the individual begins from the womb
God’s relationship with humans starts only at adulthood
Salvation is unrelated to God’s covenant promises
God’s promises are conditional on human works alone
questions.correctAnswer: God’s covenant care and hope for the individual begins from the womb
questions.explanation: Verse 9 says, 'But thou art he that took me out of the womb: thou didst make me hope,' indicating God’s intimate, covenantal involvement from the earliest life stages.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially evident in Psalms 22:25?
options: Faithfulness
Wrath
Immutability
Omnipotence
questions.correctAnswer: Faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verse 25 speaks of the psalmist fulfilling vows before God’s people, reflecting God's faithfulness that motivates human praise and vow-keeping.

questions.question: What synthesis about divine help and human helplessness do Psalms 22:11 and 20 teach?
options: When no help is available from others, God’s intervention is the only hope for deliverance
Human help is sufficient and God’s aid is unnecessary
Divine help is random and unpredictable
Help must be earned and cannot be freely granted by God
questions.correctAnswer: When no help is available from others, God’s intervention is the only hope for deliverance
questions.explanation: Verse 11 laments 'there is none to help,' and verse 20 appeals to God to 'Deliver my soul from the sword,' teaching that God’s help is essential when human aid fails.

questions.question: How does Psalms 22:30-31 contribute to the biblical theology of generational faithfulness?
options: It affirms that God’s covenant promises extend through successive generations who serve Him
Faith is only relevant to the current generation and not passed on
Generational faithfulness is unnecessary in God’s plan
God’s promises are limited to individuals, not families or nations
questions.correctAnswer: It affirms that God’s covenant promises extend through successive generations who serve Him
questions.explanation: Verse 30 says, 'A seed shall serve him; it shall be accounted to the Lord for a generation,' and verse 31 continues the theme of future proclamation, emphasizing covenant continuity.
